name: Minhocão
description: A 19th-century Brazilian cryptid reported chiefly in southern Brazil — described as a vast subterranean black-scaled worm or eel-like creature blamed for tunnels, trenches, and toppled trees — investigated by Auguste de Saint-Hilaire (1846) and Fritz Müller (1877–1878) and now generally treated as a folkloric explanation of soil-erosion and slumping events.
origin: Reports concentrate in southern Brazil (especially Santa Catarina and Paraná around Curitibanos), with secondary reports in Goiás and São Paulo; Saint-Hilaire's accounts also included locations such as Padre Aranda and Lake Feia.
